To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the permeability properties (i.e. the ability to let certain particles through while rejecting others) of a biopolymeric hydrogel can be modulated by electrostatic interactions.
the permeability properties and the barrier function of a mucus hydrogel can be modulated by electrostatic interactions between the diffusing particles and the mucin polymers.
the translocation of microscopic particles through a reconstituted mucus barrier can be modulated by varying particle surface charge and mucus concentration, and by changing buffer conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how biological functional entities control the passage of macromolecular entities.
the characterization and control of the permeability of biological functional entities such as mucus.
the fundamental principles which regulate the selective permeability of biological barriers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

mucin hydrogells are a complex barrier that can be tuned by a wide range of parameters to allow for the uptake of nutrients and drugs, and to prevent the uptake of pathogens and other undesired entities.
the permeability properties are not only a function of particle size and charge, but also of mucin concentration, ionic strength, pH and other factors.
the permeability properties and barrier function of a mucin hydrogel can be tuned by a wide range of parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the permeability properties in mucus are controlled by electrostatic interactions between the diffusing particles and the mucus polymers.
the permeability properties in mucin hydrogell can be controlled by electrostatic interactions between mucin polymers and diffusing particles.
the permeability properties can be controlled by the charge of the particle and the charge of the gel, as well as by the ionic strength of the buffer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the permeability properties and the barrier functions of biopolymer-based gels can be tuned by the chemical and structural properties of the gel and by the physicochemical environment of the system.

the permeability properties and thus the function of mucus can be modulated by the interplay between the physicochemical properties of the mucus and the particles that are to be transported through the mucin barrier.
the permeability barrier function of a biopolymeric hydrogel such as mucus is highly tunable.
